result_semantic_payload.summary: Settlement-log vs CRM reconciliation (read-only). The evidence set is a small file artifact (3 files, no Windows-native telemetry): /crm/orders.csv (4 CRM orders), /payments/settlements.log (4 settlement lines) and /README.txt which states the linkage rule — "Settlements reference CRM order ids verbatim. A settlement whose order id does not exist in the CRM table cannot be treated as the same order." Linkage key = order_id (verbatim string match), corroborated by amount equality. CONFIRMED (3): ORD-70231 (wangqiang, 20000 USDT, paid) ↔ settlement 2024-06-01 order=ORD-70231 wallet=TXabc111 amount=20000 ok; ORD-70232 (zhaolei, 15000, paid) ↔ 2024-06-01 order=ORD-70232 wallet=TXdef222 amount=15000 ok; ORD-70233 (sunli, 31500, paid) ↔ 2024-06-02 order=ORD-70233 wallet=TXghi333 amount=31500 ok. MUST STAY SEPARATE (2): (a) settlement 2024-06-02 order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 ok — no CRM order ORD-72033 exists; the id is a near-duplicate of ORD-70233 (digit transposition 70233→72033) and its amount 9999 ≠ 31500, so it must NOT be merged with ORD-70233; (b) CRM order ORD-70234 (qianer, 8000, cancelled) — no settlement line references it, so it is unconfirmed by the processor. Amounts are recorded without currency labels in the settlement log (CRM column is amount_usdt); wallet identifiers (TXabc111, TXdef222, TXghi333, TXjkl444) exist only in the settlement log and have no CRM-side counterpart, so wallet↔buyer attribution is not evidenced. No prior analyses exist for this task; no registry/event-log/prefetch sources were available, so no Windows-native corroboration was possible.

claim_candidates.text: The reconciliation key between CRM orders and payment-processor settlements is the order_id field, matched verbatim; README.txt states settlements reference CRM order ids verbatim and that a settlement whose order id is absent from the CRM table cannot be treated as the same order.

CRM order ORD-70231 (buyer wangqiang, 20000, status paid) is confirmed by the settlement log line '2024-06-01 settle order=ORD-70231 wallet=TXabc111 amount=20000 ok', linked by verbatim order_id match with corroborating amount equality (20000).

CRM order ORD-70232 (buyer zhaolei, 15000, status paid) is confirmed by the settlement log line '2024-06-01 settle order=ORD-70232 wallet=TXdef222 amount=15000 ok', linked by verbatim order_id match with corroborating amount equality (15000).

CRM order ORD-70233 (buyer sunli, 31500, status paid) is confirmed by the settlement log line '2024-06-02 settle order=ORD-70233 wallet=TXghi333 amount=31500 ok', linked by verbatim order_id match with corroborating amount equality (31500).

The settlement log line '2024-06-02 settle order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 ok' must be kept separate from all CRM orders: no CRM order with id ORD-72033 exists, so per the README rule it cannot be treated as the same order as any CRM record.

Settlement ORD-72033 must not be merged with CRM order ORD-70233 despite the similar id: the ids differ by digit transposition (70233 vs 72033) and the amounts differ (9999 vs 31500), so both the primary key and the corroborating amount field fail.
limitations: Inference from id-string and amount comparison; no processor-side documentation of ORD-72033's origin is present in the evidence set.

claim_candidates.text: CRM order ORD-70234 (buyer qianer, 8000, status cancelled) is not confirmed by the settlement log: no settlement line references ORD-70234, so it must remain separate from the confirmed set.

Wallet identifiers TXabc111, TXdef222, TXghi333 and TXjkl444 appear only in the settlement log; the CRM table has no wallet column, so wallet-to-buyer attribution is not evidenced and must not be asserted from this data alone.

limitations: Scope note: the delegated source scope 'windows' contains no Windows-native artifacts in this task; the available evidence is /README.txt, /crm/orders.csv and /payments/settlements.log only, so conclusions are limited to those file contents.
No registry, event-log, prefetch, amcache, shellbag, account or terminal evidence was present; execution and device-activity corroboration was therefore not possible.
File timestamps are all identical (1790594136) and reflect artifact creation, not real transaction chronology; the 2024-06-01/2024-06-02 dates are log-internal text only.
Settlement amounts lack a currency/unit label; numeric equality with CRM amount_usdt is treated as corroboration but unit equivalence is assumed.
Wallet identifiers appear only in the settlement log; buyer-to-wallet attribution is not evidenced.
The linkage rule is taken from README.txt, an in-scene document; no independent processor-side schema or documentation corroborates it.
No prior analyses or claims existed to cross-check against; no external source was consulted.
warnings: Scope/platform mismatch: the task metadata reports no platform scenario and the 'windows' scope holds only three flat files, so Windows-specific investigation rules could not be exercised.
Near-duplicate order ids (ORD-70233 vs ORD-72033) are a merge hazard; they were kept separate because both the id key and the amount field disagree.
File contents were read via preview hydration; the artifacts are small (153/263/283 bytes) and appear complete, but no checksum (md5 empty) is available to prove integrity.
